subject: REVERSE function
notes:
Printed folio 908 (PDF page 938) re-rendered and read independently: the format is `FUNCTION REVERSE ( argument-1 )` with FUNCTION and REVERSE both UNDERLINED (required), one unbracketed required operand, no optional phrase. Grammar: functionCall : FUNCTION functionName (LPAREN functionArgList? RPAREN)? ; REVERSE is NOT a lexer token (only REVERSE_VIDEO and REVERSED are - grep-verified over Grammar/) so it arrives as IDENTIFIER through functionName. The catalog row is Fixed 1..1 and the arity gate was re-run live against the built CLI: `FUNCTION REVERSE` (no parens) -> COBOL1504 '1 argument(s); 0 given'; `FUNCTION REVERSE()` -> COBOL1504 '0 given'; `FUNCTION REVERSE(W-A W-B)` -> COBOL1504 '2 given'; `FUNCTION REVERSE(OMITTED)` -> COBOL1544 (8.4.3.2.3 SR7, cite-checked). The parens being syntactically optional in the grammar is harmless: the shape is still REJECTED, at bind time rather than parse time. TRANSCRIPTION REPAIRED (wave 60, kb/Work PB1536): specs/ISO_COBOL.md 15.78.2 had rendered this format as bare Markdown text with no 
 block and no  markup, unlike every neighbour; printed folio 908 (PDF page 938) was re-rendered and the format restored as 
`FUNCTION REVERSE ( argument-1 )`
. The rule-digest changed with that markup only - the format's content (two required words, one required operand) is unchanged, so this verdict is RESTATED, not re-derived. The repair is what the new CatalogCoverageDriftTests.EveryFmtRow_CarriesADiagramOrAFormatLabel gate holds. ⚠ Test coverage is POSITIVE-ONLY: both test-refs write the correct one-argument format (StringFamily_PinnedToSpec has an InlineData `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE("abc 12") TO T.`; IF134A carries 109 REVERSE references, e.g. `MOVE FUNCTION REVERSE("figure") TO WS-ANUM.`), so acceptance is pinned, but NO test pins the four rejection shapes above - they were verified by hand. A negative golden for arity 0/2 and OMITTED is test-needed.
